subject: Mayoral and School Committee Candidate Forum
overview: The Medford Ward 6 Democratic Committee hosted a mayoral and school committee candidate forum ahead of the 2017 municipal election. Candidates presented platforms focusing on infrastructure, school facility maintenance, special education, and public safety priorities.

items.title: Introduction and Procedures
items.summary: Moderators Henry Miller and Julia Novia opened the forum, explained the timing rules for candidate statements, and noted candidate Paulette van der Kloot’s absence due to illness.

items.title: Mayoral Candidate Statement: David McKillop
items.summary: Challenger David McKillop proposed eliminating parking kiosks, increasing DPW staffing for infrastructure, and constructing a new police and fire station.

items.title: Mayoral Candidate Statement: Stephanie Muccini Burke
items.summary: Incumbent Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke highlighted the city's high bond rating, the Complete Streets initiative, and the ongoing planning for a new police station.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Robert Skerry
items.summary: Robert Skerry advocated for a five-year master facilities plan and the continued integration of vocational and academic programs at the high school campus.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Alexis Rodriguez
items.summary: Alexis Rodriguez proposed improving parent-committee communication by assigning individual committee members to act as dedicated liaisons for specific schools.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Mea Quinn Mustone
items.summary: Incumbent Mea Quinn Mustone highlighted her efforts to resolve bus overcrowding and expressed support for a master plan to manage school building maintenance.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Angela Moore
items.summary: Angela Moore called for prioritized career and technical education and a proactive yearly maintenance schedule for all school facilities.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Michael Ruggiero
items.summary: Michael Ruggiero suggested scheduling committee meetings on weekends to increase accessibility and advocated for addressing socio-economic disparities between schools.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Erin DiBenedetto
items.summary: Incumbent Erin DiBenedetto emphasized her experience in special education and the need to expand online learning opportunities for students.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Kathy Kreatz
items.summary: Incumbent Kathy Kreatz discussed the success of the city's vocational robotics programs and the importance of conducting direct classroom observations.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Kathleen Cullinane
items.summary: Kathleen Cullinane advocated for increased special education funding and updated drug awareness programs to address the opioid crisis.

items.title: School Committee Candidate Statement: Paul Ruseau
items.summary: Paul Ruseau recommended a comprehensive K-12 computer science curriculum and prioritized maintenance based on safety and educational impact over aesthetics.

items.title: Forum Closing
items.summary: Moderators concluded the event by reminding citizens of the October 18 voter registration deadline and announcing an upcoming City Council candidate forum.
